title: On the commodity page Frontend labels each species tick box with its Latin name alone; Design release 1 labels it with the common name and the Latin name in brackets, for example "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)".

finding.frontend: Every tick box on the commodity page is labelled with a Latin name and nothing else — "Bison bison", "Bos spp.", "Bos taurus", "Bubalus bubalis", "Equus caballus", "Felis catus", "Canis lupus familiaris", "Salmo salar". A common name appears only in the fieldset legend for the commodity the species sits under ("Cow (0102)"), never on the box itself. The species record the view model reads carries only a value and a text, with no slot for a common name at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:6-13). A user who knows the animal as a cow, a dog or a salmon never sees that word next to the box they have to tick.
finding.prototype: Every species row in the results panel reads as its common name with the Latin name in brackets, and the rule holds for every species rather than for the ones the fixture happens to name: where a species carries its own common name the row is "<common name> (<Latin name>)", and where it does not the commodity's name is used instead, so "Cyprinidae" renders as "Ornamental fish (Cyprinidae)" (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:11-17). The captured results panel shows "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)". The same pairing is what the search matches against, so typing "cattle" finds Bos taurus (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:51-55).
finding.difference: Label the species tick boxes on the commodity page "<common name> (<Latin name>)", falling back to the commodity's own name where the species has no common name of its own. This needs the reference data to carry a common name per species: the commodities service exposes only a value and a text per species and has no real client behind the stub (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/index.js:37-42, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:15-26), so whether this is copy work or a reference-data change turns on what the live commodity service returns. Banded as frontend work because the rendering is the part that is wrong today; if the live service turns out not to carry a common name per species, the band moves to needs-backend. Scope it to the tick-box labels only: the species heading on the commodity-details page is the Latin name on both sides, and changing it would move Frontend away from Design release 1 rather than towards it.
finding.falsifiedBy: A frontend species tick-box label that already reads as a common name — for instance the live commodity service returning "Domestic cattle" rather than "Bos taurus" in the species text — which would make this a fixture difference rather than a labelling one.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (capture/html/frontend/fe-commodity-search.html, fe-consignment-details.html, capture/html/prototype/dr1-what-are-you-importing-results.html, dr1-consignment-details.html) and both 2x page shots. Read the cited label builder at app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:11-17 and the matcher at :51-54, and traced the requirements side's commodity-details species heading from app/views/consignment-details.html:100 back to app/routes.js:704. Rubric point 6 fired — the finding asked Frontend to change something the requirements side does the same way — and the claim has been narrowed to the commodity page.
finding.correction:
The claim was half right and has been narrowed. What was claimed: that Frontend labels species by Latin name alone on both the commodity page and the commodity-details page, and that both should be changed to " ()". What is true: the commodity page half stands exactly — the captured DOM shows eight tick boxes labelled with Latin names only, against a captured requirements-side results row reading "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)". The commodity-details half is wrong. Design release 1 sets that page's species heading from species.speciesName, which is the raw Latin label (app/routes.js:704, rendered at app/views/consignment-details.html:100), and its captured page shows

Bos taurus

— character for character what Frontend renders at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.njk. The two sides agree there, so asking Frontend to change it would have moved it away from the signed-off design. fe-consignment-details and dr1-consignment-details have been dropped from the screens list and the difference slot now says explicitly to leave that heading alone. Note for whoever picks this up: the requirements side does carry a common name on the commodity-details entry (app/routes.js:702) and chooses not to render it — the Latin-only heading is a decision, not an omission. Two citations were also a line out and have been corrected: the commodities service accessors are at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/index.js:37-42, and the stub species map runs to line 26.

relatedTo.why: Design release 1's search matches on the common name, so a search built without common names in the data would answer only half the hint it prints.
